graphFor moved from graph/index.ts into graph/-private.ts when #8755 flattened the graph package; 5.9.1 still exports the same function under the same name from the private graph entry (and the @ember-data/graph/-private shim forwards it).
peekGraph moved with graphFor into graph/-private.ts in #8755; same function, same name, exported from the private graph entry at 5.9.1.
The diffArray helper was deleted by #8550 (remove 4.x deprecations) together with the computed-chains code that used it; 5.x has no array diff helper in its surface.

The ManyArray class became the LegacyManyArray interface (the runtime object is built by the store), exported as ManyArray from @warp-drive/legacy/model. It continues the declaration in type positions; value uses such as instanceof have no successor, which the type-only report says.

modelForMixin moved into the legacy package with #10005 but is no longer exported: 5.9.1 exports no _modelForMixin from any model entry. It was an internal helper for mixin-based polymorphic lookups; nothing public replaces it.

LifetimesConfig was the options type of LifetimesService; #9444 renamed the service to CachePolicy (now DefaultCachePolicy) and its options type to PolicyConfig, which keeps apiCacheSoftExpires and apiCacheHardExpires and adds more fields. Exported as a type from @warp-drive/core/store.

The SkipCache symbol moved from the request package private types into the shared request types (core/src/types/request.ts) when the types were split per package in #9032; same symbol, same name, same role.

The BooleanTransform class moved with the serializer package into @warp-drive/legacy (#9292 onwards) and became a named export of the public transform entry; same class, same serialize/deserialize role.

peekCache(identifier) returned the per-identifier cache instance; #10055 removed it with the cache-utils module because a 5.x store has one cache, reachable as store.cache, which is different calling code rather than an import rewrite.

notifyArray(arr) dirtied the internal tag of a 4.x IdentifierArray; #9965 replaced the tag with signals. The nearest function, notifyInternalSignal in @warp-drive/core/signals/-leaked, takes a signal rather than an array, so it is not an import rewrite.
constructResource is the same function in the same file, exported by name instead of as default since 5.4; the 5.0.1 release simply did not export it, which broke the pairwise chain.

The Tag type of the 4.x tracking package went away with #9965 (universal reactivity hooks); 5.x keeps its signal type internal and lets an app plug its reactivity in through SignalHooks and setupSignals from @warp-drive/core/configure.
